title: Home care after a stroke
also: caring for a bedridden stroke patient
what: A guide for family: how to help a person at home after a stroke, safely and without extra risks.
why: When a person has been discharged home after a stroke.
duration: recovery usually takes months; care is needed every day
tell_doctor: If there is trouble swallowing or coughing while eating
If pressure sores or red skin appear
All the medicines the person takes

prepare.title: Home
prepare.text: Remove rugs and cords, and put grab bars in the bathroom and toilet.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Give them exactly as prescribed. Do not stop them on your own.

prepare.title: Exercises
prepare.text: Ask the rehabilitation specialist which exercises to do at home.

steps: If the person lies in bed, turn them every 2 hours
Check the skin on the heels, tailbone and shoulder blades every day
Feed them sitting up, in small portions, without rushing
Help with the exercises the specialist showed
Encourage them to do everything they can by themselves
Measure blood pressure and write it down
feel: Recovery is slow and uneven. This is normal
Caring is tiring. Family also need rest and help
after: Go to follow-up visits with the doctor
Keep an eye on blood pressure and blood sugar
If it is hard to cope, ask about help from social services
red_flags: New weakness of an arm or leg, a drooping face, trouble speaking: call your local emergency number
Sudden severe headache or loss of consciousness: call your local emergency number
Coughing and choking while eating, fever: see a doctor urgently

faq.a: Usually in the first months. But improvement can continue for longer.

faq.q: How can another stroke be prevented?
faq.a: Take medicines as prescribed, control blood pressure, and stop smoking and drinking alcohol.

reminders.text: Time to turn them and check the skin. Write blood pressure in the diary.
